rows.what_to_do_or_say:
“Squad, fall in.”
“Squad, stand at ease.”
rows.action:
Form the squad with reference to Table 2-1-6. 
Ensure the squad is properly dressed, spaced and facing the trainer.

rows.what_to_do_or_say: “The first drill is Sedi-A, which means Position of Attention.”
rows.action:
Explain that attention is the basic position for all stationary drills. 
Emphasise smartness, stillness, alertness and eyes to the front.

rows.what_to_do_or_say:
“Watch my demonstration, without explanation.” Do not follow. Command: Sedi-A

“Watch my demonstration, with explanation.” On the command Sedi-A.” Refer to 2-1-4

“Watch my demonstration in stages with explanation.” Refer to Table 2-1-5
rows.action:
[Without explanation] Trainer demonstrates the full movement into the position of attention without explanation.
 
[With explanation] Trainer demonstrates again while explaining the key points of posture, stillness, alertness and smartness. 

[In stages] Trainer breaks the movement into stages, highlighting common errors such as moving after the command, poor posture or unnecessary movement.

rows.what_to_do_or_say:
“What is the meaning of Sedi-A?”

“What are the key points when standing at attention?”
rows.action: Check understanding. Refer to Table 2-1-4 & 2-1-5 for expected answers.

rows.what_to_do_or_say:
“Squad, on my command, execute Sedi-A.”

Command: Sedi-A

“The command to repeat the drill is: Semula – As you were.”
rows.action: Squad practices the movement. Trainer checks posture, timing, stillness and smartness. Correct common mistakes immediately and repeat.

Form the squad with reference to Table 2-1-11.

Ensure the squad are alert and ready to receive the command.

rows.what_to_do_or_say:
“The next drill is At Ease.”

“The command Senang Di-Ri means Stand at Ease.”

“The command Rehatkan Diri means Stand Easy.” This drill allows the soldier to relax slightly, but discipline must still be maintained.”
rows.action:
Explain the difference between Stand at Ease and Stand Easy. 
Emphasise that soldiers must still remain in position and listen for next command.

[In stages] Trainer breaks the movement into stages, highlighting common errors and reinforces discipline, posture and reaction to command.

rows.what_to_do_or_say: “Squad, Sedi-A”
rows.action:
Form the squad with reference to Table 2-1-18. 
Start the squad from the position of attention. 
Ensure there is enough space between soldiers to prevent contacts during turns.,

rows.what_to_do_or_say:
“The next drill is Turning During Halt.”

“The three commands are:”

Ke-Kanan Pu-Sing – Right Turn
Ke-Kiri Pu-Sing – Left Turn 
Ke-Belakang Pu-Sing – About Turn

“You will turn only on the executive word …Sing.”
rows.action:
Explain that turning during halt is used to change direction while remaining in position. 
Emphasise sharpness, balance, correct direction and timing.

rows.what_to_do_or_say:
“Watch my demonstration, without explanation.” Do not follow. 

Command: Ke-Kanan Pu-Sing Command: Ke-Kiri Pu-Sing
Command: Ke-Belakang Pu-Sing
Command: Seporah Ke-Kanan/ Ke-Kiri Pu-sing


“Watch my demonstration, with explanation.” Refer to 2-1-14


“Watch my demonstration in stages with explanation.” Refer to Table 2-1-15 to 2-1-17
rows.action:
[Without explanation] Trainer demonstrates Right Turn, Left Turn and About Turn without explanation. 
[With explanation] Trainer demonstrates again each turn and explains the direction, timing and final position.
[In stages] Trainer breaks the movement into stages, highlighting common error for each stage.
For a Right/ Left Incline 
Turn (45 degrees).

rows.what_to_do_or_say:
“What is the command for Right Turn?”

“What is the command for Left Turn?”

“What is the command for About Turn?”
rows.action: Check understanding. Refer to Table 2-1-14 for expected answers.

rows.what_to_do_or_say:
“Squad, we will practice by command.

Command: Ke-Kanan Pu-Sing Command: Ke-Kiri Pu-Sing
Command: Ke-Belakang Pu-Sing

“The command to repeat the drill is: Semula – As you were.”
rows.action: Squad practices each turn. Trainer observes for wrong direction, poor balance, slow reaction, dragging of feet and lack of smartness. Correct and repeat until movements are correct.

grid.text: This movement teaches soldiers to pay the proper compliment to a commissioned officer or uncased Colours

Full demonstration

Saluting as a soldier can be done with different attire (uniform / plain clothes) and with/without headdress

With beret, the tip of the forefinger should touch the forehead an inch above the right eye.

With Helmet, the forefinger should touch the brim of the helmet.

Without head dress, meets or pass by an officer, he/she will stand to Attention with salute facing the officer.

If soldier is in plain clothes with head dress (other than military head dress), Soldier is to remove it and stand to Attention with salute.
Ask squad if there are any questions

grid.text:
There are two different commands for the purpose of training soldiers to dismiss or fall out from parade smartly, correctly and with discipline – maintaining composure even at the end of a drill

A squad will always dismiss in Close Order.

During training or parade, instructors state clearly whether a salute is required.

“SKUAD BERSU-RAI!” – Dismissal

There are two different commands for the purpose of training soldiers to dismiss or fall out from parade smartly, correctly and with discipline – maintaining composure even at the end of a drill

A squad will always dismiss in Close Order.

During training or parade, instructors state clearly whether a salute is required.
